sarah: FYI the vuln scanner flagged CVE-2024-XXXX in our keystore-agent base image used in private deployments. It's a kernel userspace wrapper issue, P0 from the scanner. Planning a canary patch tomorrow morning to bump to image:keystore-agent:v1.2.3 which includes the fix. Need to validate isolation + audit before rolling.

leo: Thanks. Can we do the canary in a locked-down namespace only? I suggest namespace 'priv-canary' in eu-west-1 cluster. We'll run netpols + RBAC delta and verify no audit drops. Window 08:30-09:30 UTC?

anika: 08:30 works. Checklist: 1) apply tightened netpol to prevent unexpected egress 2) patch daemonset image to v1.2.3 3) toggle rolebinding to simulate least-privilege regressions 4) run synthetic decrypt traffic and malformed tokens 5) confirm audit-forwarder saw all KMS calls with trace id and principal mapping.

leo: Netpol I'll apply will allow only DNS+KMS-proxy egress and node kubelet. Sample:```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: priv-keystore-restrict
  namespace: priv-canary
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

sarah: Good. Add a PDB minAvailable:1 so we don't kill all agents if the image has a regression. Also we need a preflight to check audit-forwarder connectivity before the patch. Quick command: `kubectl -n logging get pods -l app=audit-forwarder -o wide` and `kubectl logs -n logging -l app=audit-forwarder --tail=50`

anika: For RBAC toggle, I'd like to remove the decrypt permission from the canary svcacct and observe the authz failures surface in both the keystore logs and central audit. Command I'll use: `kubectl delete rolebinding keystore-decrypt-binding -n priv-canary --ignore-not-found=true` then reapply after test.

leo: Can we also simulate KMS throttling? A brief iptables DROP on the kms-proxy side for 30s to induce latency spikes will exercise our graceful fallback. We'll coordinate with infra.

ops-bot: created canary/priv-keystore-patch (ttl:3h) assigned_to:sarah window:2026-03-24T08:30:00Z-09:30:00Z

sec-bot: Audit requirements reminder: every KMS Encrypt/Decrypt must include fields: timestamp, request_id/X-Request-ID, principal (svcacct@ns), operation, key_id, response_code. Forwarder must return 2xx for write acknowledgement. If any forwards fail >3 times in 5m, abort canary.

sarah: I'll instrument the test harness to propagate X-Request-ID and span ids. PoC python test:```python
import requests
import uuid
for i in range(10):
    rid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    headers = {'X-Request-ID': rid}
    r = requests.post('http://keystore.priv-canary.svc.cluster.local:8080/decrypt', json={'kid': 'canary-'+str(i)}, headers=headers, timeout=5)
    print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

anika: Log checks: grep for principal mapping in node logs: `journalctl -u keystore-agent | grep principal=` and for audit-forwarder entries: `jq '.request_id, .principal, .operation, .response_code' /tmp/audit-forward.log`

leo: Rollback plan if we see dropped auditevents or >10% 5xx from keystore: 1) kubectl -n priv-canary set image daemonset/keystore-agent keystore-agent=image:keystore-agent:v1.2.2 2) kubectl -n priv-canary delete networkpolicy priv-keystore-restrict --ignore-not-found=true 3) restart audit-forwarder pods.

sec-bot: Add alerting: create a temporary Prom rule: `increase(audit_forwarder_errors_total[5m]) > 3` -> page #eng-oncall and auto-run rollback playbook.

sarah: I'll post the runbook link in #eng-security 1h before start. ping me in-thread for preflight signoffs. Thanks all. :lock:
